doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Friday the 13th and the Seder phone call
summary: Banter about Friday the 13th and Passover story.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Yeah. The 13th, is that have to do with some kind of religious thing? Was that it? What, what is it about the 13th, I wonder?
I don’t know, Jim.
I forgot. I think it has some kind of religious…
Is it? I know there are buildings in New York with no 13th floor.
Oh, yeah, I know it.
It’s a superstition, I guess.
For years, yeah. I know, but it had to do with… that was the day Jesus was nailed up or something like that, I forgot. (laughs) Instead of saying “ouch,” he said, “Man, it’s Friday the 13th.”
Well, you know, I was not raised with much religious (overlapping/inaudible).
I remember that, yeah. (laughs)
Um…
What was… they had took the Jews to Japan, right? Who did that? (laughs)
(laughs) Moses.
Moses, that’s right. (laughs) He got cheap tickets, probably. (laughs)
Well, that, that was a childhood story because you asked me what I was doing.
Oh, right, yeah. I called.
And I was preparing to go to a Seder…
Yeah.
…with my grandparents. And I asked you if you were Jewish. And you said no.
Right.
So I proceeded to tell you the story…
Right.
…for Passover, and you asked me where Moses took them, and I said they marched to Japan.
Remember the other part?
Yes. I then had to get off the phone…
‘Cause you were making Christmas cards or something?
Easter eggs.
Easter eggs, that’s right.
I was dying Easter eggs.
(laughs) That’s a very nice New York story. I like that.
